items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: it was Dick Carey and Al Hall and Jimmy Crawford, Ray Deal and Max and myself.

ctx.x: Did he double on peck horn?

He doubled on anything he could get his hands on, you know. We'd go into a place, and they had some instruments laying around. He just picked up -- it used to make Max mad, you know, because he would pick up anything and play on it, but it was Dick Carey and Al Hall and Jimmy Crawford, Ray Deal and Max and myself.

And so we were going to take a trip down in Virginia, but we had to stop off in Harrisburg -- I think that's Pennsylvania -- to play a night. So we played in Harrisburg. And so Max says, well, look, we'll hit on the road, and we'll go on down in Virginia, stop off at a motel on our way down, you know, before we get to this town in Virginia we're going to play.

items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: Eddie and I've been associated for I don't know how long. We used to live near one another

ctx.x: But Teddy Wilson never got that opportunity, and Art Tatum was blind, Sy Oliver should have done it. Don Redman -- these people had credits, you know. But what they were doing was writing for the white show without getting the

credits, because I was a copyist, and I copied a lot of these, Don Redman's things and Sy Oliver's and Luther Henderson's and for -- for name bands -- Eddie Barefield, Joe Garaggiola -- not Joe Garaggiola -- Joe Cordilla, the clarinetist. He used to be with Whiteman,
